newsitem.title: USA: Iowa soybean harvest active during week ended Sun.
newsitem.headline: Iowa soybean harvest active during week ended Sun.

text.p: Soybean harvest in Iowa was active last week, leaping to 22 percent complete, up from one percent the previous week, according to the Iowa Agricultural Statistics Service.
But the soy harvest pace remained behind the 33 percent average and behind the 25 percent pace a year ago.
Yields were favorable, ranging from the low 40's to the 60's.
Eighty-four percent of the state's crop was dropping leaves, below the 93 percent average and down from 95 percent a year ago.
Corn harvest also was active but most farmers chose to combine soybeans due to the vulnerable nature of the crop.
Corn harvest stood at five percent complete as of Sunday, up from three percent a week ago but below the 15 percent average and down from 13 percent a year ago.
Eighty-five percent of the corn crop was mature and safe from frost, the Statistics Service said.

Topsoil moisture was three percent very short, 18 percent short, 77 percent adequate and two percent surplus. Subsoil moisture was three percent very short, 28 percent short, 67 percent adequate and two percent surplus.
